entry.summary: No prior clearance for a visit of 14 days or less arriving and leaving on the same vessel, if you can support yourself. Longer stays need entry clearance in advance.
entry.max_stay: 14 days without clearance; up to 6 months with long-term entry clearance (NZ$150, about A$120 at RBA, 30 October 2026: A$1 = NZ$1.2480; apply at least 3 months ahead)

layers.process: For stays over 14 days, or business visits, send the entry clearance form to the Pitcairn Islands Office before booking passage.

laws.rule: Visits of 14 days or less arriving and leaving on the same vessel: a short-term visitor visa is given on arrival if you meet character, health, insurance and funds requirements. Longer stays need a long-term visitor visa in advance (NZ$150, medical, chest X-ray and police certificates).
Medical insurance including evacuation cover of at least US$500,000 is mandatory for visitors.

local-law.note: From the place's own government sources.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: A short-term visitor visa is issued on arrival for visits of 14 days or less on the same vessel, if you meet character, health, insurance and funds requirements; longer stays need an application in advance. Evacuation insurance of at least US$500,000 is mandatory.

steps.step: For longer stays apply to the Pitcairn Islands Government in advance.
Buy medical insurance with evacuation cover of at least US$500,000.

intellectual-property.summary: Official patents, trademarks, licensing and IP ownership in Pitcairn Islands.

facts.label: Official IP office
facts.text: The Pitcairn Islands are a UK overseas territory and are not listed as their own WIPO member in the official IP-office directory. Official UK IP law and the UK IPO are the usual starting point, together with the official Pitcairn government pages.

facts.label: Official IP office
facts.text: Patents, trademarks and related official registers start with Intellectual Property Office (United Kingdom).

facts.label: Ownership, licensing and filing
facts.text: Foreign ownership of IP, official licensing formalities, and whether the system is first-to-file, should be confirmed on the official IP office pages (and, where listed, on WIPO Lex). This pass records the official office rather than a full statute summary.
